title: S&P Global US Services PMI (final, Sep 2026 data) — 09:45 ET, 15 minutes before ISM Services
source: EST: READ VERBATIM OFF S&P GLOBAL'S OWN CALENDAR LISTING, which the proposing lane could not reach — pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, fetched direct 2026-10-05 research session 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes). Its Upcoming grid now enumerates October and carries the row verbatim: 'October 05 ... 13:45 UTC S&P Global US Services PMI' (alongside '13:45 UTC S&P Global US Sector PMI'), and 13:45 UTC is 09:45 ET under EDT. The same fetch independently corroborates the cadence on either side: 'October 01 ... 13:45 UTC S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI' (first working day) and 'September 23 ... 13:45 UTC S&P Global Flash US PMI'. This SUPERSEDES the proposal's rule-derivation (proposals/sp-global-services-pmi-2026-10-05.from-ism-services-2026-10-05.json), which inferred 10-05 from the page's own stated rule ('Services PMI: third working day') because the October rows had truncated and the page then rate-limited; the derivation and the listing agree. STILL FILED estimate, and the label is a SCHEMA GAP, not date doubt: market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed-source prefix covering a private PMI compiler (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/TSY:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:/PJM:/SEC:/OCC: all miss — CAL: is 'automated aggregator cross-ref' and this is the publisher's own primary, so claiming it would be dishonest), and this lane's hard limits permit a confirmed flip only on IR:/BLS:/FED:. The same standing gap is named by the ISM entries and the funding-deadline ledger; it is now the third lane to hit it.
notes: READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT — and the reason is measured, not asserted. This print's information is released TWELVE DAYS EARLIER: S&P Global publishes a flash estimate of the same survey (2026-09-23, 09:45 ET, on the same fetched calendar), so 10-05 carries only the revision. Revisions measured from S&P Global's own consecutive flash releases, each of which quotes the prior month's final: May 50.9→50.7 (-0.2), Jun 51.3→51.2 (-0.1), Jul 53.6→54.6 (+1.0), Aug 56.8→56.5 (-0.3); mean |revision| 0.40pt. The tape ignores them. Measured first-hand on Yahoo 5-minute bars (n=51-60 sessions, 2026-06-12..09-08), the 09:45-10:00 ET window on the two release days in sample (08-05, 09-03) ranked BELOW its own median in 9 of 10 instrument-days and at or below p25 in 7 of 10 against a 25% base rate — including 08-05, which carried the +1.0 July revision, the largest in the sample. THIS SETTLES THE CONTAMINANT QUESTION the proposing ledger opened. ism-services-2026-10-05's row 2 filed this print as 'a structural contaminant' inside the 09:20-10:30 window FT-48 and FT-ism-services-2026-11-04-1 measure ISM with. It is a calendar contaminant and a tape non-event: on the SAME two days the 10:00-10:15 ISM window ran TLT p92/p88 and ^TNX p92, while the 09:45 window sat at p13/p18 (SPY), p2/p8 (QQQ), p0 (TLT 09-03). FT-ism-services-2026-11-04-1's void clause requires a named catalyst 'shown on hourly bars to still be running at the release hour' — on this evidence naming this print should NOT void it. Full ledger: docs/research/events/sp-global-services-pmi-2026-10-05.md.
